The reported 1,320 is consistent with the erroneous 1,540 initial count (1,540 − 220 = 1,320), so the discrepancy is the same misplaced factor-of-10 error in the discovery-cell counts.

errors.explanation: The stated ceiling is incorrect for the finite-sample estimator given in Eq. 2. Moreover, for N <= k (or when all n_c are 0/1), F can reach 1. Thus 1 - 1/k is not a universal upper bound for the defined F.

errors.claim: "The flip rate has a ceiling: F\leq 1-1/k, where k is the number of claim classes."

errors.claim: "The ceiling on the flip rate is $F\leq1-1/k$ for $k$ claim classes."

errors.claim: "The ceiling on the flip rate is $F\leq1-1/k$ for $k$ claim classes."
errors.evidence: "F=1-\frac{\sum_c n_c(n_c-1)}{N(N-1)}." ... "The ceiling on the flip rate is $F\leq1-1/k$ for $k$ claim classes."
errors.explanation: For an exactly uniform assignment of N specifications into k classes (n_c = N/k), the formula gives F = 1 - (N^2/k - N)/[N(N-1)] = N(1 - 1/k)/(N-1), which is strictly greater than 1 - 1/k for finite N. For example N=10, k=2: F = 10*(1/2)/9 = 5/9 ≈ 0.555... > 1 - 1/2 = 0.5. So the stated ceiling F ≤ 1 - 1/k is incorrect except in the N→∞ limit.

errors.claim: "The ceiling on the flip rate is $F\leq1-1/k$ for $k$ claim classes."
